title: Shelter-in-place
tldr: Get inside if the outdoor hazard makes travel more dangerous, and choose the room for that hazard: a lowest-floor sturdy interior area for a tornado, protective interior mass for fallout, or few outside openings for an airborne chemical release. Close openings and control ventilation only as the hazard requires. Do not remain in a burning, flooding or collapsing building, and do not wait for a message when immediate danger is visible.
steps: Read the actual shelter instruction and affected area.
Use an interior low room for tornadoes, a basement or central area for fallout, and the room specified for a chemical event.
Take people, pets, medicines, phone power and a radio without delaying shelter.
Remain until officials advise otherwise, unless fire or another immediate danger makes the building unsafe.
next: Plan safe rooms for the hazards in your area and keep an alert source that works during outages.
watch: Do not apply chemical room-sealing instructions to every hazard or remain in a burning building.
